messages:
maya: FYI ticket #45321 — EU customer says invoice total != dashboard total by €0.02 after VAT; invoice ID inv_2026_8912. They attached a CSV export. Can someone triage?

tom_support: On it. Can you paste the CSV snippet and the exact amounts the customer sees vs our dashboard?

maya: CSV snippet from customer export:
```
request_id,currency,net_amount_eur,vat_rate,vat_amount_eur,line_total_eur
req_1001,EUR,10.01,20,2.00,12.01
req_1002,EUR,15.49,20,3.10,18.59
req_1003,EUR,8.30,20,1.66,9.96
req_1004,EUR,1200.76,20,240.15,1440.91
```
Customer says invoice total = €1481.47 but dashboard shows €1481.45.

tom_support: I pulled our billing-export for inv_2026_8912: summed net = 1234.56, summed VAT per-line = 246.91, invoice total = 1481.47. Dashboard aggregate (from metrics) calculates VAT on summed net then rounds once: VAT = round(1234.56 * 0.20, 2) = 246.91? actually dashboard shows 246.89 resulting in 1481.45. So discrepancy 0.02.

leo_finance: This smells like per-line rounding vs invoice-level rounding + possible currency conversion bucketization. In EU VAT it's common for invoice lines to be taxed and rounded per-line; some customers/systems expect VAT computed on the invoice subtotal then rounded. Both are defensible but must be consistent across surfaces. Which pipeline is applying which?

anya_eng: I reproduced locally in staging. Our ingestion pipeline currently does VAT per-item and stores vat_amount rounded to 2 decimals at ingestion time. Dashboard metrics compute VAT from unrounded stored net sums then round at display. SQL to demonstrate: 
```sql
select sum(round(vat_amount,2)) as vat_sum_lines, round(sum(net_amount)*0.20,2) as vat_invoice_level
from billing_events where invoice_id = 'inv_2026_8912';
```
Results: vat_sum_lines = 246.91, vat_invoice_level = 246.89. Difference = 0.02.

tom_support: So the CSV/invoice (customer-facing) uses per-line rounded VAT while dashboard uses invoice-level rounding. Customer saw the invoice value and expects dashboard to match.

leo_finance: For remediation: 1) For issued invoices, we should either issue a €0.02 credit or append a "rounding_adjustment" line item on the invoice explaining the carry. Prefer to issue a small credit (better UX). 2) Long term: pick a single canonical rounding policy and make both invoice export and dashboard use it. I prefer matching invoice calc (per-line) so external invoices don't surprise customers.

anya_eng: Quick mitigation I can do: modify billing-export to include an explicit rounding_adjustment column and surface it in the CSV/API. That way customers and dashboard can show identical sums (dashboard will sum line VAT + rounding_adjustment). I'll add unit tests for both sum(round(vat,2)) and round(sum(net)*rate,2) parity check and a config flag to switch policy. Estimated turnaround: small PR today, deploy tomorrow if no issues.

maya: Customer requested a correction/credit. Can finance approve an immediate manual credit of €0.02? They want it processed this week.

leo_finance: Approved. I'll create a manual credit memo CM-2026-55 for €0.02 and attach reason: "VAT rounding carryover — invoice inv_2026_8912". Filing FIN-789 to track. @anya_eng please include audit field in next export so we can avoid manual credits.

anya_eng: Will do. Plan: add rounding_adjustment (signed cents) to CSV and API response, update dashboard to include it in displayed invoice_total, and add a migration to recompute exports if needed. PR: https://git.redwood/eng/billing/pull/1246 (in review).

billing-bot: Billing export completed for inv_2026_8912 — report generated (attachments: export_1769456123.csv).

tom_support: Thanks. I'll reply to customer: confirm cause (rounding policy mismatch), offer €0.02 credit, note upcoming fix to surface rounding_adjustment on exports and dashboard so values align.

maya: Customer responded: "Thanks, credit is fine — please apply and confirm." I'll mark ticket #45321 as escalated to finance until credit done.

leo_finance: Credit issued CM-2026-55, applied to account. Marked resolved on our side.

anya_eng: Follow-ups: 1) deploy PR to add rounding_adjustment field, 2) add e2e test asserting invoice CSV total == dashboard total for sample invoices, 3) add changelog note for billing behavior. I'll schedule a post-deploy check on next billing cycle.

tom_support: Great. Closing loop with customer once we've verified dashboard and export parity. :thumbsup:
